meta.subject: AP Statistics
meta.description: Topic 9.3 practice interpreting a confidence interval for the slope of a population regression line, interpreting the confidence level, using whether 0 is in the interval to judge evidence of a linear relationship, and deciding whether a claimed slope value is plausible.

perField.ci_interpretation: Say, 'We are 95% confident...' and identify the slope of the population regression line in context.
perField.confidence_level_meaning: Think repeated random sampling: about 95% of those intervals would capture the true slope.
perField.linear_claim_choice: Check whether 0 is inside the interval and whether the interval is all positive or all negative.
perField.linear_claim_reason: Explain your conclusion by saying whether 0 is a plausible slope and what sign the interval values have.
perField.slope_claim_choice: A claimed slope is plausible if it falls inside the confidence interval.
perField.slope_claim_reason: Justify your answer by stating whether the claimed slope value is contained in the interval.
